claim: TRIM37 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase mutated in Mulibrey nanism.
source: TRIM37 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase mutated in Mulibrey nanism, a disease with impaired organ growth and increased tumor formation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by citations in the introduction (Kallijärvi et al., 2005; Kallijärvi et al., 2002).

claim: Mulibrey nanism is a disease with impaired organ growth and increased tumor formation.
source: TRIM37 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase mutated in Mulibrey nanism, a disease with impaired organ growth and increased tumor formation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Avela et al., 2000; Karlberg et al., 2009).

claim: TRIM37 depletion from tissue culture cells results in supernumerary foci bearing the centriolar protein Centrin.
source: TRIM37 depletion from tissue culture cells results in supernumerary foci bearing the centriolar protein Centrin.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data shown in Figure 1 and previous work (Balestra et al., 2013).

claim: An atypical de novo assembly pathway can generate Cenpas that act as microtubule-organizing centers (MTOCs).
source: Here, we characterize these centriolar protein assemblies (Cenpas) to uncover the mechanism of action of TRIM37. We find that an atypical de novo assembly pathway can generate Cenpas that act as microtubule-organizing centers (MTOCs), including in Mulibrey patient cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 1F-G and Figure 2.

claim: Cenpas act as microtubule-organizing centers (MTOCs) in Mulibrey patient cells.
source: We find that an atypical de novo assembly pathway can generate Cenpas that act as microtubule-organizing centers (MTOCs), including in Mulibrey patient cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: Correlative light electron microscopy reveals that Cenpas are centriole-related or electron-dense structures with stripes.
source: Correlative light electron microscopy reveals that Cenpas are centriole-related or electron-dense structures with stripes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by CLEM data in Figure 3.

claim: TRIM37 regulates the stability and solubility of Centrobin.
source: TRIM37 regulates the stability and solubility of Centrobin, which accumulates in elongated entities resembling the striped electron dense structures upon TRIM37 depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 4H-K showing protein stability and Figure 4I showing solubility changes.

claim: Centrobin accumulates in elongated entities resembling the striped electron dense structures upon TRIM37 depletion.
source: TRIM37 regulates the stability and solubility of Centrobin, which accumulates in elongated entities resembling the striped electron dense structures upon TRIM37 depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 4A-B and Figure 4F-G comparing U-ExM and TEM structures.

claim: Cenpas formation upon TRIM37 depletion requires PLK4.
source: Furthermore, Cenpas formation upon TRIM37 depletion requires PLK4, as well as two parallel pathways relying respectively on Centrobin and PLK1.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6A-B showing that PLK4 inhibition prevents Cenpas formation.

claim: Cenpas formation upon TRIM37 depletion requires two parallel pathways relying respectively on Centrobin and PLK1.
source: Furthermore, Cenpas formation upon TRIM37 depletion requires PLK4, as well as two parallel pathways relying respectively on Centrobin and PLK1.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6E showing that simultaneous Centrobin depletion and PLK1 inhibition completely prevents Cenpas formation.

claim: Centrioles are small evolutionarily conserved cylindrical organelles characterized by nine triplets of microtubules arranged with a striking ninefold radial symmetry.
source: Centrioles are small evolutionarily conserved cylindrical organelles characterized by nine triplets of microtubules (MTs) arranged with a striking ninefold radial symmetry (reviewed in Gönczy and Hatzopoulos, 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a review citation.

claim: Centrioles are essential for the formation of cilia.
source: Centrioles are essential for the formation of cilia and also recruit pericentriolar material (PCM), including the MT nucleator γ-tubulin ring complex, thus forming the centrosome of animal cells (reviewed in Bornens, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a review citation.

claim: Centrioles recruit pericentriolar material (PCM), including the MT nucleator γ-tubulin ring complex, thus forming the centrosome of animal cells.
source: Centrioles are essential for the formation of cilia and also recruit pericentriolar material (PCM), including the MT nucleator γ-tubulin ring complex, thus forming the centrosome of animal cells (reviewed in Bornens, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a review citation.

claim: Most cycling cells have two centrioles at cell cycle onset and four centrioles by the time of mitosis.
source: Probably because of such important roles, centriole number is tightly regulated, with most cycling cells having two units at cell cycle onset and four units by the time of mitosis (reviewed in Sullenberger et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a review citation.

claim: Supernumerary centrioles lead to extra cilia and centrosomes.
source: Thus, supernumerary centrioles lead to extra cilia and centrosomes (Duensing et al., 2007; Habedanck et al., 2005; Mahjoub and Stearns, 2012), which can be observed also in several human disease conditions, including certain cancer types (reviewed in Bettencourt-Dias et al., 2011; Chavali et al., 2014; Gönczy, 2015; Nigg and Holland, 2018; Nigg and Raff, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Supernumerary centrioles can be observed in several human disease conditions, including certain cancer types.
source: Thus, supernumerary centrioles lead to extra cilia and centrosomes (Duensing et al., 2007; Habedanck et al., 2005; Mahjoub and Stearns, 2012), which can be observed also in several human disease conditions, including certain cancer types (reviewed in Bettencourt-Dias et al., 2011; Chavali et al., 2014; Gönczy, 2015; Nigg and Holland, 2018; Nigg and Raff, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by review citations.

claim: The mother centriole is at least two cell generations old.
source: The two resident centrioles present at the onset of the cell cycle differ in their age: whereas the older, mother, centriole is at least two cell generations old, the younger, daughter, centriole was formed in the previous cell cycle.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established knowledge about centriole biology.

claim: The daughter centriole was formed in the previous cell cycle.
source: The two resident centrioles present at the onset of the cell cycle differ in their age: whereas the older, mother, centriole is at least two cell generations old, the younger, daughter, centriole was formed in the previous cell cycle.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established knowledge about centriole biology.

claim: The mother centriole bears distinctive distal and sub-distal appendages that the daughter centriole acquires only later during the cell cycle.
source: The mother centriole bears distinctive distal and sub-distal appendages that the daughter centriole acquires only later during the cell cycle (reviewed in Sullenberger et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a review citation.

claim: In human cells, the proximal region of both mother and daughter centrioles in the G1 phase of the cell cycle is encircled by a torus bearing the interacting proteins CEP57/CEP63/CEP152.
source: In human cells, the proximal region of both mother and daughter centrioles in the G1 phase of the cell cycle is encircled by a torus bearing the interacting proteins CEP57/CEP63/CEP152 (Brown et al., 2013; Cizmecioglu et al., 2010; Hatch et al., 2010; Lukinavičius et al., 2013; Sir et al., 2011) (reviewed in Banterle and Gönczy, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: PLK4 is recruited to the torus and focuses to a single location toward the G1/S transition, marking the site of procentriole assembly.
source: The Polo-like-kinase PLK4 is recruited to this torus, where it focuses to a single location toward the G1/S transition, owing notably to a protective interaction with its substrate STIL, thus marking the site of procentriole assembly (Klebba et al., 2015; Moyer et al., 2015; Ohta et al., 2014) (reviewed in Arquint and Nigg, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The onset of procentriole assembly entails the formation of a ninefold radially symmetric cartwheel thought to act as a scaffold for the entire organelle.
source: The onset of procentriole assembly entails the formation of a ninefold radially symmetric cartwheel thought to act as a scaffold for the entire organelle (reviewed in Guichard et al., 2018; Hirono, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by review citations.

claim: HsSAS-6 is the fundamental building block of the cartwheel.
source: The fundamental building block of the cartwheel is HsSAS-6, the homologues of which can self-assemble in vitro into ninefold radially symmetric structures akin to those found in vivo (Guichard et al., 2017; Kitagawa et al., 2011b; Strnad et al., 2007; van Breugel et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Homologues of HsSAS-6 can self-assemble in vitro into ninefold radially symmetric structures akin to those found in vivo.
source: The fundamental building block of the cartwheel is HsSAS-6, the homologues of which can self-assemble in vitro into ninefold radially symmetric structures akin to those found in vivo (Guichard et al., 2017; Kitagawa et al., 2011b; Strnad et al., 2007; van Breugel et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: During S/G2, the emerging procentriole remains closely associated with the resident centriole and elongates through the contribution of the centriolar proteins CPAP/SAS-4, SPICE, and C2CD3.
source: During S/G2, the emerging procentriole remains closely associated with the resident centriole and elongates, notably through the contribution of the centriolar proteins CPAP/SAS-4, SPICE, and C2CD3 (Balestra et al., 2013; Comartin et al., 2013; Kohlmaier et al., 2009; Schmidt et al., 2009; Tang et al., 2009; Thauvin-Robinet et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: During mitosis, the procentriole disengages from the resident centriole in a manner that requires the activity of PLK1.
source: During mitosis, the procentriole disengages from the resident centriole in a manner that requires the activity of the Polo-like-kinase PLK1 (Loncarek et al., 2010; Tsou et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Excess PLK1 during S or G2 leads to premature centriole disengagement and centriole reduplication.
source: Excess PLK1 during S or G2 leads to premature centriole disengagement and centriole reduplication (Loncarek et al., 2010; Tsou et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Disengagement during mitosis generates two centriolar units that are licensed to recruit PCM and to trigger a new round of centriole assembly in the following cell cycle.
source: Normally, disengagement during mitosis generates two centriolar units that are thus licensed to recruit PCM and to trigger a new round of centriole assembly in the following cell cycle.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established knowledge about centriole biology.

claim: De novo centriole assembly occurs when the protist Naegleria gruberi transitions from an acentriolar amoeboid life form to a flagellated mode of locomotion.
source: Such de novo assembly occurs in some physiological conditions, for instance when the protist Naegleria gruberi transitions from an acentriolar amoeboid life form to a flagellated mode of locomotion (Fritz-Laylin et al., 2016; Fulton and Dingle, 1971).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Centrioles assemble de novo at the blastocyst stage in rodent embryos.
source: Likewise, centrioles assemble de novo at the blastocyst stage in rodent embryos (Courtois et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: De novo assembly of centrioles can be triggered experimentally in human cells following removal of resident centrioles through laser ablation or chronic treatment with the PLK4 inhibitor Centrinone followed by drug release.
source: De novo assembly of centrioles can also be triggered experimentally in human cells following removal of resident centrioles through laser ablation or chronic treatment with the PLK4 inhibitor Centrinone followed by drug release (Khodjakov et al., 2002; Wong et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: In human cells de novo assembly is normally silenced by the resident centrioles.
source: These findings demonstrate that in human cells de novo assembly is normally silenced by the resident centrioles.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is an inference from the cited experimental findings.

claim: Experimentally provoked de novo centriole assembly in human cells is error prone and lacks number control.
source: Moreover, in contrast to the situation in physiological conditions, experimentally provoked de novo centriole assembly in human cells is error prone and lacks number control (La Terra et al., 2005; Wong et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Upon depletion of RMB14 or Neurl4, human cells assemble foci de novo that contain some centriolar proteins and which can function as MTOCs.
source: Furthermore, upon depletion of the intrinsically disordered protein RMB14 or the Neuralized Homology repeat containing protein Neurl4, human cells assemble foci de novo that contain some centriolar proteins and which can function as MTOCs (Li et al., 2012; Shiratsuchi et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: TRIM37 is a RING-B-box-coiled-coil protein with E3 ubiquitin ligase activity.
source: TRIM37 is a RING-B-box-coiled-coil protein with E3 ubiquitin ligase activity (Kallijärvi et al., 2005; Kallijärvi et al., 2002), which somehow prevents the formation of foci bearing centriolar markers (Balestra et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: TRIM37 prevents the formation of foci bearing centriolar markers.
source: TRIM37 is a RING-B-box-coiled-coil protein with E3 ubiquitin ligase activity (Kallijärvi et al., 2005; Kallijärvi et al., 2002), which somehow prevents the formation of foci bearing centriolar markers (Balestra et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Individuals with loss-of-function mutations in both copies of TRIM37 are born with Mulibrey nanism.
source: Individuals with loss-of-function mutations in both copies of TRIM37 are born with a rare disorder known as Mulibrey nanism (Muscle-liver-brain-eye nanism).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established knowledge about the genetic basis of Mulibrey nanism.

claim: The main features of Mulibrey nanism are growth failure with prenatal onset, as well as characteristic dysmorphic traits and impairment in muscle, liver, brain, and eye.
source: The main features of this disorder are growth failure with prenatal onset, as well as characteristic dysmorphic traits and impairment in those organs that give rise to the name of the condition (Avela et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Mulibrey patients have a high probability of developing several tumor types.
source: In addition, Mulibrey patients have a high probability of developing several tumor types (Karlberg et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Mice lacking Trim37 recapitulate several features of Mulibrey nanism, including a higher propensity to form tumors.
source: Mice lacking Trim37 recapitulate several features of Mulibrey nanism, including a higher propensity to form tumors (Kettunen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: TRIM37 mono-ubiquitinates and thereby stabilizes PEX5, promoting peroxisomal function in tissue culture cells.
source: In tissue culture cells, TRIM37 mono-ubiquitinates and thereby stabilizes PEX5, promoting peroxisomal function (Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Trim37 knock out mice and mouse cell lines depleted of Trim37 do not exhibit peroxisomal associated phenotype.
source: However, Trim37 knock out mice and mouse cell lines depleted of Trim37 do not exhibit peroxisomal associated phenotype (Wang et al., 2017), suggesting that the conserved pathological features exhibited by the mouse disease model must have a different cellular etiology.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: The chromosomal region 17q23 where TRIM37 resides is amplified in ~40% of breast cancers.
source: The chromosomal region 17q23 where TRIM37 resides is amplified in ~40% of breast cancers (Sinclair et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: TRIM37 mono-ubiquitinates histone H2A in the MCF-7 breast cancer cell line.
source: TRIM37 mono-ubiquitinates histone H2A in the MCF-7 breast cancer cell line, and this has been reported to dampen the expression of thousands of genes, including tumors suppressors, thus offering a potential link between TRIM37 overexpression and tumorigenesis (Bhatnagar et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: TRIM37 mono-ubiquitination of histone H2A dampens the expression of thousands of genes, including tumor suppressors.
source: TRIM37 mono-ubiquitinates histone H2A in the MCF-7 breast cancer cell line, and this has been reported to dampen the expression of thousands of genes, including tumors suppressors, thus offering a potential link between TRIM37 overexpression and tumorigenesis (Bhatnagar et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: TRIM37 overexpression has been linked to increased cell invasion and metastasis in colorectal and hepatocellular carcinoma.
source: Furthermore, TRIM37 overexpression has been linked to increased cell invasion and metastasis in colorectal and hepatocellular carcinoma (Hu and Gan, 2017; Jiang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Cancer cells overexpressing TRIM37 are hypersensitive to the absence of centrioles upon treatment with the PLK4 inhibitor Centrinone.
source: Cancer cells overexpressing TRIM37 are hypersensitive to the absence of centrioles upon treatment with the PLK4 inhibitor Centrinone, because excess TRIM37 interferes with acentriolar spindle assembly, inducing mitotic failure (Meitinger et al., 2020; Yeow et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Excess TRIM37 interferes with acentriolar spindle assembly, inducing mitotic failure.
source: Cancer cells overexpressing TRIM37 are hypersensitive to the absence of centrioles upon treatment with the PLK4 inhibitor Centrinone, because excess TRIM37 interferes with acentriolar spindle assembly, inducing mitotic failure (Meitinger et al., 2020; Yeow et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Cancer cells overexpressing TRIM37 assemble small condensates harboring the centrosomal proteins CEP192 and CEP152, as well as inactive PLK4.
source: Moreover, such cells assemble small condensates harboring the centrosomal proteins CEP192 and CEP152, as well as inactive PLK4 (Meitinger et al., 2020; Meitinger et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The absence of TRIM37 triggers the formation of larger condensates containing PLK4.
source: Interestingly, in addition, the absence of TRIM37 triggers the formation of larger condensates containing PLK4 (Meitinger et al., 2020; Meitinger et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Both depletion and excess of TRIM37 is accompanied by detrimental cellular consequences.
source: Overall, both depletion and excess of TRIM37 is accompanied by detrimental cellular consequences.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is an inference from the cited literature.

claim: A genome-wide siRNA-based screen identified TRIM37 as a potent negative regulator of Centrin-1:GFP foci number.
source: We previously performed a genome-wide siRNA-based screen in human cells to identify regulators of centriole assembly, using the number of foci harboring the centriolar marker Centrin-1:GFP as a readout (Balestra et al., 2013). In this screen, we identified TRIM37 as a potent negative regulator of Centrin-1:GFP foci number.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: ~50% of cells depleted of TRIM37 possessed supernumerary foci harboring the centriolar proteins Centrin and CP110.
source: Our initial characterization of the TRIM37 depletion phenotype revealed that ~50% of cells possessed supernumerary foci harboring the centriolar proteins Centrin and CP110.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and refers to previous work (Balestra et al., 2013).

claim: Instances of multipolar spindle assembly and chromosome miss-segregation were observed upon TRIM37 depletion.
source: Moreover, instances of multipolar spindle assembly and chromosome miss-segregation were observed.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and refers to previous work (Balestra et al., 2013).

claim: Inhibition of PLK1 partially suppressed supernumerary foci formation upon TRIM37 depletion.
source: Additionally, we found that inhibition of PLK1 partially suppressed supernumerary foci formation upon TRIM37 depletion, leading to the suggestion that such foci occurred through centriole reduplication (Balestra et al., 2013), although the fact that suppression was only partial indicated that an additional explanation was to be found.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and refers to previous work (Balestra et al., 2013).

claim: Extra Centrin-1:GFP foci can appear in the vicinity of resident centrioles (8/13 foci) upon TRIM37 depletion.
source: As shown in Figure 1A, we found that extra Centrin-1:GFP foci can appear in the vicinity of resident centrioles (yellow arrows, 8/13 foci), as well as far from them (orange arrows, 5/13 foci).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by live imaging data in Figure 1A.

claim: Extra Centrin-1:GFP foci can appear far from resident centrioles (5/13 foci) upon TRIM37 depletion.
source: As shown in Figure 1A, we found that extra Centrin-1:GFP foci can appear in the vicinity of resident centrioles (yellow arrows, 8/13 foci), as well as far from them (orange arrows, 5/13 foci).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by live imaging data in Figure 1A.

claim: Extra Centrin-1:GFP foci upon TRIM37 depletion may form both through centriole reduplication and some type of de novo process.
source: These results suggest that extra Centrin-1:GFP foci upon TRIM37 depletion may form both through centriole reduplication and some type of de novo process.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the live imaging data.

claim: TRIM37 depletion using siRNA was near complete in HC1 cells and HeLa cells.
source: Western blot analyses established that TRIM37 depletion using siRNA was near complete both in HC1 cells and in HeLa cells used hereafter (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The intensity of extra Centrin-1:GFP foci was typically weaker than that of regular centrioles, especially in the early assembly stages.
source: Note that the intensity of extra Centrin-1:GFP foci was typically weaker than that of regular centrioles, especially in the early assembly stages.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 1A and is an observation from the imaging data.

claim: ~90% of extra Centrin-1:GFP foci in TRIM37-depleted cells did not harbor CEP63 or HsSAS-6.
source: Strikingly, in cells depleted of TRIM37, we found that in addition to the normal four Centrin-1:GFP foci accompanied by two Cep63 foci and two HsSAS-6 foci,~90% of extra Centrin-1:GFP foci did not harbor CEP63 or HsSAS-6 (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1B,C.

claim: >90% of extra Centrin-1:GFP foci in RO3306-treated cells harbored CEP63 and/or HsSAS-6.
source: For comparison, we likewise analyzed cells arrested in G2 following treatment with the CDK1 inhibitor RO3306, which induces PLK1-dependent centriole reduplication (Loncarek et al., 2010). In this case, >90% of extra Centrin-1:GFP foci harbored CEP63 and/or HsSAS-6 (Figure 1B,C), in contrast to the situation upon TRIM37 depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1B,C.

claim: TRIM37 does not act solely to prevent centriole reduplication.
source: These findings further indicate that TRIM37 does not act solely to prevent centriole reduplication.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the comparison of TRIM37 depletion and RO3306 treatment data.

claim: Supernumerary Centrin-2/CP110 foci appeared principally as individual units at the 24 hr time point after TRIM37 depletion.
source: Upon TRIM37 depletion, we found that supernumerary Centrin-2/CP110 foci appeared principally as individual units at the 24 hr time point, but that pairs of foci became more frequent thereafter (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1D,E.

claim: Pairs of supernumerary Centrin-2/CP110 foci became more frequent after 24 hr following TRIM37 depletion.
source: Upon TRIM37 depletion, we found that supernumerary Centrin-2/CP110 foci appeared principally as individual units at the 24 hr time point, but that pairs of foci became more frequent thereafter (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1D,E.

claim: Supernumerary Centrin-2/CP110 foci can trigger further rounds of centriole assembly.
source: These results indicate that supernumerary Centrin-2/CP110 foci can trigger further rounds of centriole assembly.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the time course data showing pairs of foci forming.

claim: Both TRIM37:GFP and TRIM37:NES:GFP equally rescued the TRIM37 depletion phenotype.
source: We found that both TRIM37:GFP and TRIM37:NES:GFP equally rescued the TRIM37 depletion phenotype (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B), indicating that TRIM37 acts outside the nucleus to prevent Cenpas formation.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: TRIM37 acts outside the nucleus to prevent Cenpas formation.
source: We found that both TRIM37:GFP and TRIM37:NES:GFP equally rescued the TRIM37 depletion phenotype (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B), indicating that TRIM37 acts outside the nucleus to prevent Cenpas formation.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the rescue experiment with nuclear export signal fusion.

claim: Only ~10% of G1 cells harbored centrosomal TRIM37:GFP.
source: This enabled us to establish that whereas only ~10% of G1 cells harbored centrosomal TRIM37:GFP,~60% of S/G2 cells did so (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E.

claim: ~60% of S/G2 cells harbored centrosomal TRIM37:GFP.
source: This enabled us to establish that whereas only ~10% of G1 cells harbored centrosomal TRIM37:GFP,~60% of S/G2 cells did so (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E.

claim: TRIM37:GFP partially overlapped with CEP164.
source: We also localized the fusion protein with respect to CEP63, Centrin-2 and the distal appendage protein CEP164, finding that TRIM37:GFP partially overlapped with CEP164 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by high magnification confocal images in Figure 1—figure supplement 2F,G.

claim: TRIM37 localizes to the distal part of centrioles.
source: Overall, we conclude that TRIM37 localizes to the distal part of centrioles; it will be interesting to investigate whether TRIM37 acts from this location to prevent the formation of at least some Cenpas, perhaps those near resident centrioles.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the colocalization data with CEP164.

claim: TRIM37 depletion resulted in an increased frequency of mitotic cells with more than two MTOCs.
source: We found that whereas most control mitotic cells harbored two MTOCs, TRIM37 depletion resulted in an increased frequency of cells with more than two MTOCs, which often differed in size (Figure 1F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by microtubule regrowth data in Figure 1F,G.

claim: ~40% of Cenpas did not nucleate microtubules.
source: In addition, we found that ~40% of Cenpas did not nucleate microtubules, indicative of some compositional heterogeneity (Figure 1F, siTRIM37, inset 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by microtubule regrowth data in Figure 1F.

claim: Microtubules nucleated from Cenpas contribute to the aberrant spindle assembly and chromosome miss-segregation phenotypes of TRIM37-depleted cells.
source: Overall, we conclude that microtubules nucleated from Cenpas contribute to the aberrant spindle assembly and chromosome miss-segregation phenotypes of TRIM37-depleted cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the MTOC data.

claim: Western blot analysis showed essentially no detectable TRIM37 protein in Mulibrey patient cells.
source: As reported in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E, western blot analysis showed essentially no detectable TRIM37 protein in patient cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Mulibrey patient cells in mitosis harbored supernumerary Centrin-2 foci, some of which were positive for γ-tubulin.
source: Echoing the results in tissue culture cell lines depleted of TRIM37, we found that patient cells in mitosis harbored supernumerary Centrin-2 foci, some of which were positive for γ-tubulin (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2A,B.

claim: Patient fibroblasts with Cenpas frequently harbored pseudo-bipolar (~25% of cases) and multipolar (~31% of cases) spindles during metaphase.
source: During metaphase, the spindle was invariably bipolar in control fibroblasts, whereas patient fibroblasts with Cenpas frequently harbored pseudo-bipolar (~25% of cases) and multipolar (~31% of cases) spindles (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2C–E.

claim: Mitotic spindles were predominantly bipolar (~87% of cases) by anaphase in patient fibroblasts.
source: These aberrant figures were corrected in most cases by anaphase, when mitotic spindles were predominantly bipolar (~87% of cases) (Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2F,G.

claim: Chromosome segregation defects revealed by chromosome bridges or lagging chromosomes were observed in ~16% of patient cells with a bipolar anaphase spindle.
source: Importantly, however, even such spindles were not fully functional: chromosome segregation defects revealed by chromosome bridges or lagging chromosomes were observed in ~16% of patient cells with a bipolar anaphase spindle (Figure 2F,H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2F,H.

claim: Micronuclei were present in ~9% of interphase patient fibroblasts.
source: Moreover, micronuclei were present in ~9% of interphase patient fibroblast (Figure 2I,J).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by DAPI staining data in Figure 2I,J.

claim: Cenpas are present and active in Mulibrey patient cells, thus contributing to genome instability.
source: Overall, we conclude that Cenpas are present and active in Mulibrey patient cells, thus contributing to genome instability.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the patient cell data showing Cenpas, aberrant spindles, and chromosome segregation defects.

claim: ~23% of TRIM37-depleted cells possessed extra acetylated tubulin foci.
source: We stained cells depleted of TRIM37 with antibodies against acetylated tubulin, a signature modification of centriolar microtubules, finding that ~23% cells possessed extra acetylated tubulin foci (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Some Cenpas formed upon TRIM37 depletion harbored merely Centrin1:GFP, but neither acetylated tubulin nor CEP152.
source: We found that some of the Cenpas formed upon TRIM37 depletion harbored merely Centrin1:GFP, but neither acetylated tubulin nor CEP152 (Figure 3B–D, yellow arrows).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by U-ExM data in Figure 3B–D.

claim: Some Cenpas were positive for Centrin1:GFP, acetylated tubulin, and CEP152.
source: By contrast, other Cenpas were positive for all three markers (Figure 3C–E), with the acetylated tubulin signal being sometimes smaller than normal (Figure 3C,D, white arrows).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by U-ExM data in Figure 3C–E.

claim: Some Cenpas appeared to have matured into entities with seemingly regular acetylated tubulin and CEP152 signals.
source: Moreover, some Cenpas appeared to have matured into entities with seemingly regular acetylated tubulin and CEP152 signals (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by U-ExM data in Figure 3E.

claim: Cenpas are heterogeneous in nature, with partially overlapping composition.
source: Together, these findings support the notion that Cenpas are heterogeneous in nature, with partially overlapping composition.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the U-ExM data showing different marker combinations.

claim: CLEM analysis uncovered 22 unusual structures in eight TRIM37-depleted cells.
source: In addition, this analysis uncovered 22 unusual structures (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CLEM data.

claim: Ten unusual structures were variable centriole-related electron-dense assemblies that harbored microtubules, but only partially resembled centrioles.
source: Ten of these were variable centriole-related electron-dense assemblies that harbored microtubules, but only partially resembled centrioles (Figure 3I,K,L; Figure 3—figure supplement 1I,J,L,N,O,P).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CLEM data in Figure 3.

claim: Twelve unusual structures were elongated electron-dense striped entities, referred to as 'tiger structures'.
source: Strikingly, the remaining 12 unusual structures were elongated electron-dense striped entities, hereafter referred as 'tiger structures' (Figure 3J,M; Figure 3—figure supplement 1H,U).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CLEM data in Figure 3.

claim: An individual tiger structure sometimes correlated with more than one Centrin-1:GFP focus.
source: We noted also that an individual tiger structure sometimes correlated with more than one Centrin-1:GFP focus (Figure 3—figure supplement 1U).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CLEM data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1U.

claim: The ultrastructure of Cenpas formed upon TRIM37 depletion is somewhat heterogeneous, perhaps reflecting different pathways or steps in their assembly.
source: Overall, we conclude that the ultrastructure of Cenpas formed upon TRIM37 depletion is somewhat heterogeneous, perhaps reflecting different pathways or steps in their assembly.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the CLEM data showing different types of structures.

claim: Centrobin is present in elongated assemblies in the cytoplasm upon TRIM37 depletion.
source: Strikingly, this analysis revealed notably that Centrobin, which normally localizes tightly to the daughter centriole and to procentrioles (Zou et al., 2005), is present in elongated assemblies in the cytoplasm upon TRIM37 depletion (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4A,B.

claim: ~80% of TRIM37-depleted cells usually bore one or two Centrobin assemblies.
source: We found that ~80% of TRIM37-depleted cells usually bore one or two such Centrobin assemblies (Figure 4C; Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), and that all cells harboring Cenpas had Centrobin assemblies (n = 150), with Cenpas often colocalizing with them (~79%).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification data in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: All cells harboring Cenpas had Centrobin assemblies (n = 150), with Cenpas often colocalizing with them (~79%).
source: We found that ~80% of TRIM37-depleted cells usually bore one or two such Centrobin assemblies (Figure 4C; Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), and that all cells harboring Cenpas had Centrobin assemblies (n = 150), with Cenpas often colocalizing with them (~79%).
evidence: This is stated in the results and represents quantification of colocalization.

claim: SPICE localized to Centrobin assemblies.
source: Moreover, while most centriolar proteins tested did not localize to Centrobin assemblies (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and C–E), we found that SPICE did, although it was not needed for the formation of Centrobin assemblies (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F,G.

claim: SPICE was not needed for the formation of Centrobin assemblies.
source: Moreover, while most centriolar proteins tested did not localize to Centrobin assemblies (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and C–E), we found that SPICE did, although it was not needed for the formation of Centrobin assemblies (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data showing Centrobin assemblies form even when SPICE is depleted.

claim: PLK4 is detected in Centrobin assemblies.
source: Furthermore, we uncovered that PLK4 is also detected in Centrobin assemblies, which therefore likely coincide with the large PLK4 condensates that form in TRIM37-knock out RPE-1 cells (TRIM37-ko) (Meitinger et al., 2020; Meitinger et al., 2016; Figure 4—figure supplement 1H; Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Centrobin assemblies likely coincide with the large PLK4 condensates that form in TRIM37-knock out RPE-1 cells.
source: Furthermore, we uncovered that PLK4 is also detected in Centrobin assemblies, which therefore likely coincide with the large PLK4 condensates that form in TRIM37-knock out RPE-1 cells (TRIM37-ko) (Meitinger et al., 2020; Meitinger et al., 2016; Figure 4—figure supplement 1H; Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the colocalization data and previous reports.

claim: Centrobin assemblies generated upon TRIM37 depletion formed even when PLK4 was targeted using siRNAs.
source: Just like for SPICE, we found that Centrobin assemblies generated upon TRIM37 depletion formed even when PLK4 was targeted using siRNAs (Figure 4D,E), despite the presence of monopolar mitotic figures attesting to the efficiency of depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4D,E.

claim: The size of Centrobin assemblies was slightly diminished upon PLK4 depletion.
source: However, the size of Centrobin assemblies was slightly diminished upon PLK4 depletion (Figure 4D; Figure 4—figure supplement 1I,J; see Discussion).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1I,J.

claim: Depletion of Centrobin by siRNAs precluded formation of large PLK4 condensates.
source: By contrast, depletion of Centrobin by siRNAs precluded formation of large PLK4 condensates (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4D,E.

claim: U-ExM coupled to STED revealed that Centrobin assemblies were striated.
source: Strikingly, the superior resolution afforded by U-ExM coupled to STED revealed that such Centrobin assemblies were striated (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by U-ExM STED data in Figure 4F.

claim: The inter-stripe distances of Centrobin assemblies were analogous to those of the tiger structures unveiled through CLEM.
source: Suggestively, the inter-stripe distances of these Centrobin assemblies were analogous to those of the tiger structures unveiled through CLEM (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification data in Figure 4G.

claim: Centrobin is a constituent of the electron-dense tiger structures observed by TEM upon TRIM37 depletion.
source: In summary, U-ExM analysis strongly suggests that Centrobin is a constituent of the electron-dense tiger structures observed by TEM upon TRIM37 depletion, and raises the possibility that such structures serve as platforms for Cenpas formation.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the comparison of U-ExM and TEM data.

claim: Tiger structures may serve as platforms for Cenpas formation.
source: In summary, U-ExM analysis strongly suggests that Centrobin is a constituent of the electron-dense tiger structures observed by TEM upon TRIM37 depletion, and raises the possibility that such structures serve as platforms for Cenpas formation.
evidence: This is stated in the results and represents speculation based on the data.

claim: Real time quantitative PCR experiments showed a slight diminution in Centrobin mRNA levels upon TRIM37 depletion.
source: Performing real time quantitative PCR experiments showed a slight diminution in Centrobin mRNA levels upon TRIM37 depletion (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A), suggesting that regulation is not at the transcriptional level.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qPCR data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: TRIM37 regulation of Centrobin is not at the transcriptional level.
source: Performing real time quantitative PCR experiments showed a slight diminution in Centrobin mRNA levels upon TRIM37 depletion (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A), suggesting that regulation is not at the transcriptional level.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the qPCR data showing only slight changes in mRNA.

claim: Western blot analysis uncovered that Centrobin protein levels were slightly increased upon TRIM37 depletion.
source: By contrast, western blot analysis uncovered that Centrobin protein levels were slightly increased upon TRIM37 depletion (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by western blot data in Figure 4H.

claim: The increase in Centrobin protein level upon TRIM37 depletion was most pronounced in the insoluble fraction.
source: Accordingly, fractionating cell lysates into soluble and insoluble fractions, we found that the increase in Centrobin protein levels was most pronounced in the latter (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by fractionation western blot data in Figure 4I.

claim: The insoluble pool of Centrobin appeared to migrate slower in the gel upon TRIM37 depletion, suggestive of some posttranslational modification.
source: We noted also that the insoluble pool of Centrobin appeared to migrate slower in the gel upon TRIM37 depletion, suggesting that TRIM37 not only restricts Centrobin levels, but also might somehow regulate its posttranslational state.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an observation from the western blot data in Figure 4I.

claim: TRIM37 depletion increased Centrobin protein stability.
source: As reported in Figure 4J and K, we found that TRIM37 depletion increased Centrobin protein stability.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by cycloheximide chase data in Figure 4J and K.

claim: Centrobin overexpression generates aggregates that did not resemble the Centrobin assemblies uncovered upon TRIM37 depletion.
source: However, although Centrobin overexpression generates aggregates (Jeong et al., 2007), we found that such aggregates did not resemble the Centrobin assemblies uncovered here, nor did they trigger Cenpas formation (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Centrobin overexpression did not trigger Cenpas formation.
source: However, although Centrobin overexpression generates aggregates (Jeong et al., 2007), we found that such aggregates did not resemble the Centrobin assemblies uncovered here, nor did they trigger Cenpas formation (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: TRIM37 overexpression did not alter Centrobin centrosomal distribution.
source: In addition, TRIM37 overexpression did not alter Centrobin centrosomal distribution (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: TRIM37 normally regulates Centrobin stability, preventing the protein from forming the elongated assemblies that are invariably present in cells with Cenpas.
source: Regardless, we conclude that TRIM37 normally regulates Centrobin stability, preventing the protein from forming the elongated assemblies that are invariably present in cells with Cenpas.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the stability and assembly data.

claim: Centrobin assemblies are present in the majority of Mulibrey patient fibroblasts.
source: Importantly, we found that this was the case in the majority of cells (Figure 5A,B), with most Centrobin assemblies being associated with Cenpas (~88%, N = 150).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 5A,B.

claim: Most Centrobin assemblies in patient fibroblasts were associated with Cenpas (~88%, N = 150).
source: Importantly, we found that this was the case in the majority of cells (Figure 5A,B), with most Centrobin assemblies being associated with Cenpas (~88%, N = 150).
evidence: This is stated in the results and represents quantification of colocalization in patient cells.

claim: Centrobin assemblies are present and usually coincident with active MTOCs during mitosis in patient fibroblasts.
source: Furthermore, we found that Centrobin assemblies are present and usually coincident with active MTOCs during mitosis in patient fibroblasts (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 5C,D.

claim: The appearance of elongated Centrobin assemblies precedes that of Cenpas.
source: Initially most cells with elongated Centrobin assemblies lacked Cenpas, whereas at later time point cells with both Centrobin assemblies and Cenpas became more prevalent (Figure 5E,F). Therefore, the appearance of elongated Centrobin assemblies precedes that of Cenpas, compatible with the notion that the former is needed for the latter.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by time course data in Figure 5E,F.

claim: Elongated Centrobin assemblies are needed for Cenpas formation.
source: Initially most cells with elongated Centrobin assemblies lacked Cenpas, whereas at later time point cells with both Centrobin assemblies and Cenpas became more prevalent (Figure 5E,F). Therefore, the appearance of elongated Centrobin assemblies precedes that of Cenpas, compatible with the notion that the former is needed for the latter.
evidence: This is an inference from the time course data showing temporal precedence.

claim: siRNA-mediated depletion of Centrobin did not impact centriole assembly in HeLa Kyoto cells.
source: In our hands, siRNA-mediated depletion of Centrobin did not impact centriole assembly in HeLa Kyoto cells either, despite near-complete protein depletion (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Centrobin assemblies disappeared entirely from cells doubly depleted of Centrobin and TRIM37.
source: As anticipated, Centrobin assemblies disappeared entirely from cells doubly depleted of Centrobin and TRIM37 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Cenpas number was significantly lowered in cells doubly depleted of Centrobin and TRIM37 compared to cells depleted of TRIM37 alone.
source: Importantly, we found that Cenpas number was significantly lowered in such doubly depleted cells compared to cells depleted of TRIM37 alone (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Cenpas formation upon TRIM37 depletion was only partially prevented by Centrobin siRNA treatment.
source: Interestingly, however, even if Centrobin depletion was complete as judged by western blot analysis (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E,F), Cenpas formation upon TRIM37 depletion was only partially prevented by Centrobin siRNA treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Upon TRIM37 depletion Centrobin assemblies act as a platform seeding the formation of some, but not all, Cenpas.
source: Together, these results support the view that upon TRIM37 depletion Centrobin assemblies act as a platform seeding the formation of some, but not all, Cenpas.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the partial suppression data.

claim: Cenpas did not form when cells were grown in the presence of Centrinone for 5 days and then depleted of TRIM37 for 3 days in the continued presence of Centrinone.
source: To test the role of PLK4 kinase activity, HeLa cells were grown in the presence of Centrinone for 5 days and then depleted of TRIM37 for 3 days in the continued presence of Centrinone. We found that Cenpas did not form under these conditions, demonstrating an essential role for PLK4 kinase activity (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification data in Figure 6A and B.

claim: PLK4 kinase activity is essential for Cenpas formation upon TRIM37 depletion.
source: We found that Cenpas did not form under these conditions, demonstrating an essential role for PLK4 kinase activity (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the Centrinone treatment data.

claim: Depletion of STIL, CPAP, or SPICE did not dramatically modify the number of Cenpas upon TRIM37 depletion.
source: However, depletion of STIL, CPAP, or SPICE did not dramatically modify the number of Cenpas upon TRIM37 depletion (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification data in Figure 6A.

claim: HsSAS-6 depletion reduced Cenpas number, albeit less so than upon Plk4 inactivation.
source: By contrast, HsSAS-6 depletion reduced Cenpas number, albeit less so than upon Plk4 inactivation (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification data in Figure 6A.

claim: Some Cenpas formed upon TRIM37 depletion in HsSAS-6-ko cells, although to a lesser extent than following depletion of TRIM37 alone.
source: Although HsSAS-6-ko cells invariably lacked centrioles (Figure 6A,B), some Cenpas nevertheless formed upon TRIM37 depletion, although to a lesser extent than following depletion of TRIM37 alone (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 6A,B.

claim: Elongated Centrobin assemblies were generated unabated upon TRIM37 depletion in cells treated with Centrinone or lacking HsSAS-6.
source: In agreement with the absence of HsSAS-6 in elongated Centrobin assemblies (see Figure 4—figure supplement 1E) and the fact that PLK4 depletion does not impact such assemblies (see Figure 4D), we found that elongated Centrobin assemblies were generated unabated upon TRIM37 depletion in cells treated with Centrinone or lacking HsSAS-6 (Figure 6C,D; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 6C,D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: PLK4 activity and HsSAS-6 act downstream of, or in parallel to, Centrobin in the pathways leading to Cenpas formation upon TRIM37 depletion.
source: We conclude that PLK4 activity and HsSAS-6 act downstream of, or in parallel to, Centrobin in the pathways leading to Cenpas formation upon TRIM37 depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the data showing Centrobin assemblies form even when PLK4 or HsSAS-6 are absent.

claim: Simultaneous Centrobin depletion and PLK1 inhibition completely prevented Cenpas formation upon TRIM37 depletion.
source: Importantly, we found that simultaneous Centrobin depletion and PLK1 inhibition completely prevented Cenpas formation (Figure 6E), indicating that PLK1 and Centrobin act in parallel to promote Cenpas formation upon TRIM37 depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification data in Figure 6E.

claim: PLK1 and Centrobin act in parallel to promote Cenpas formation upon TRIM37 depletion.
source: Importantly, we found that simultaneous Centrobin depletion and PLK1 inhibition completely prevented Cenpas formation (Figure 6E), indicating that PLK1 and Centrobin act in parallel to promote Cenpas formation upon TRIM37 depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the complete suppression with double treatment.

claim: Cenpas generated upon combined TRIM37 depletion and PLK1 inhibition rarely harbored HsSAS-6.
source: Indeed, we found that Cenpas generated upon combined TRIM37 depletion and PLK1 inhibition, which thus rely strictly on Centrobin, rarely harbored HsSAS-6 (Figure 6F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 6F,G.

claim: Cenpas generated upon double depletion of TRIM37 and Centrobin frequently harbored HsSAS-6.
source: By contrast, Cenpas generated upon double depletion of TRIM37 and Centrobin, which thus rely strictly on PKL1, frequently harbored HsSAS-6 (Figure 6F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 6F,G.

claim: Two pathways are triggered when TRIM37 is lacking: one that relies on elongated Centrobin assemblies that act as a platform to assemble Cenpas, and another one mediated by PLK1 that operates through HsSAS-6 recruitment.
source: Taken together, our findings indicate that two pathways are triggered when TRIM37 is lacking: one that relies on elongated Centrobin assemblies that act as a platform to assemble Cenpas, which at the least is initially independent of HsSAS-6, and another one mediated by PLK1 that operates through HsSAS-6 recruitment (Figure 6H, see Discussion).
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the combined data on Centrobin and PLK1 pathways.

claim: The Centrobin pathway for Cenpas formation is initially independent of HsSAS-6.
source: Taken together, our findings indicate that two pathways are triggered when TRIM37 is lacking: one that relies on elongated Centrobin assemblies that act as a platform to assemble Cenpas, which at the least is initially independent of HsSAS-6, and another one mediated by PLK1 that operates through HsSAS-6 recruitment (Figure 6H, see Discussion).
evidence: This is stated in the results and is an inference from the data showing Cenpas can form without HsSAS-6 when relying on Centrobin.
